---
title: "Existing semantic annotations"
---

```{r setup}
source("_common.R")
ann <- targets::tar_read(annotation_summary, store = store)
```

EML 2.2 supports semantic annotations on datasets, entities, and attributes.
Where they exist, they are a **partial gold standard** for what attributes
measure. Vocabulary is inferred from the value URI.

## Vocabularies by subject level

```{r vocabularies}
plotly::plot_ly(
  ann$vocabularies,
  x = ~vocabulary, y = ~annotations, color = ~subject_level, type = "bar"
) |>
  plotly::layout(barmode = "stack", yaxis = list(title = "Annotations", type = "log"))
interactive_table(ann$vocabularies, "annotation_vocabularies")
```

## Properties

```{r properties}
interactive_table(ann$properties, "annotation_properties", columns = list(property_uri = wide(320)))
```

## Non-QUDT annotation values

Most QUDT annotations restate the unit. Values from other vocabularies show
what ecological characteristics are already being recorded.

```{r values}
interactive_table(ann$values, "annotation_values", columns = list(value_uri = wide(320)))
```

## "Contains measurements of type" values and their units

These annotations link a measured characteristic (often ECSO) directly to an
attribute. They show which units carry each characteristic in practice.

```{r measured-types}
interactive_table(
  ann$measured_types, "annotation_measured_types",
  columns = list(value_uri = wide(300), units = wide(320))
)
```
